stages.note: The corpus carries 5 literal role markers in 3 documents — ghost tags are created by the renderer, not inherited from the data. Across 1,000 turns, rendering as chatml costs 18.0 extra tokens per turn. That is only 0.8% of this corpus because a reasoning trace averages 2,220 tokens per turn; on short chat turns the same markers are the double-digit waste the session describes.

stages.name: Language ID

grading.protocol: trained on FLORES-200 dev, graded on devtest — disjoint sentence sets
limits: FLORES is clean, edited, single-language prose from one domain; web crawl is none of those, so this is an upper bound, not an estimate of field accuracy.
Only languages in FLORES-200 can be detected at all. Bodo (brx) is in our corpus and absent from FLORES, so its documents are unadjudicable rather than mislabelled.
Accuracy is reported per document length because the five-sentence figure flatters the detector; one sentence is the honest number for short web text.
grading.note: 9 of these languages share the Devanagari script, so a script detector cannot separate them at all — its accuracy is the chance baseline, not a weak result.

stages.note: 1,580 documents disagree with the language their folder claims. 76 were left undecided rather than guessed, and 6,735 are unadjudicable because their claimed language has no FLORES profile — a limit of the detector, not a defect in the corpus. Nothing is dropped here: a mislabelled document is a finding about the source, not a document to delete.

stages.name: Quality filter

residual_bias.note: Script-aware rules narrow the gap but do not close it. Two reasons, both worth naming: the Devanagari stop-word list is built from Hindi and under-serves Maithili and Bodo, which is the same bias one level down; and `mean_word_length` in [3, 10] was tuned on English web prose, so it also cuts agglutinative Telugu and LaTeX-heavy reasoning traces.

classifier_gate.note: No FineWeb-Edu model exists here. This is a transparent function of the rule outcomes, off by default, and never reported as measured.

stages.note: Dropped 12,354 documents on script-aware rules; the published English thresholds would have dropped 23,492 — 11,138 more, almost all well-formed Indic text failing rules that ask for English full stops and English stop words. Even script-aware, survival is uneven: 82% of English-language documents against 41% of Indic ones.

stages.name: Deduplicate

params.note: The session quotes this preset as target ~0.75; the banding approximation gives 0.719. We publish what the code computes.

stages.note: Removed 766 documents: 85 byte-identical and 681 near-duplicates at a similarity threshold of 0.719. LSH proposed 1,279 candidate pairs and the true Jaccard confirmed 783 — banding is a recall device, not a verdict.

stages.name: PII scrub

patterns.why: local-part, @, domain with a dot — near-perfect precision in practice
requires a country code, separators, or an Indian mobile prefix

known_false_positives: 2.6.21.7 — a Linux kernel version. Every octet is a legal byte, so no pattern can separate this from a real address. Only context could, and a regex has none.

patterns.why: twelve digits in three spaced groups
known_false_positives: any 4-4-4 digit grouping, such as a spaced card number

patterns.why: five letters, four digits, one letter — the Indian PAN shape

name_layer.note: No NER model has usable Maithili or Dogri support, so this is a declared stand-in rather than a model. No precision or recall is published: there is no gold set, and inventing one would be the same error as running a fake classifier.
